text_blocks.snippet: Low blood pressure, also known as hypotension, can be caused by various factors, including dehydration, heart conditions, certain medications, and endocrine problems. It can also be a result of severe infections, allergic reactions, or severe pain. In some cases, low blood pressure can be related to pregnancy, prolonged bed rest, or even psychological factors.
snippet_highlighted_words: dehydration, heart conditions, certain medications, and endocrine problems

text_blocks.snippet: Here's a more detailed look at the causes:

list.snippet: Insufficient water intake reduces blood volume, leading to lower blood pressure.
Fever, vomiting, severe diarrhea, and strenuous exercise can also cause dehydration.
Conditions like abnormally low heart rate, heart valve problems, heart attacks, and heart failure can affect the heart's ability to pump enough blood, resulting in hypotension.
These conditions can prevent the body from quickly pumping more blood when standing up.

Some medications, especially those used to treat high blood pressure, heart failure, erectile dysfunction, neurological problems, and depression, can lower blood pressure as a side effect, according to Cleveland Clinic.
Drugs like diuretics, beta-blockers, and tricyclic antidepressants are also known to cause hypotension.
Conditions like underactive thyroid (hypothyroidism), Addison's disease (adrenal insufficiency), and low blood sugar (hypoglycemia) can disrupt the body's ability to regulate blood pressure.
Diabetes can also damage the nerves that control blood pressure, potentially leading to hypotension.

list.title: Severe infections:
list.snippet: Septic shock, caused by bacteria entering the bloodstream, can lead to dangerously low blood pressure.

list.title: Allergic reactions:
list.snippet: Anaphylactic shock, a severe allergic reaction, can cause a sudden drop in blood pressure.

list.title: Pain:
list.snippet: Severe pain can trigger the body to release hormones that dilate blood vessels, causing blood pressure to drop.

list.title: Nervous system disorders:
list.snippet: Conditions like Parkinson's disease can affect the nervous system's ability to regulate blood pressure.

list.title: Nutritional deficiencies:
list.snippet: A lack of essential vitamins like B-12 and folic acid can lead to anemia, which can contribute to low blood pressure, says newyorkcardiac.com.

list.title: Pregnancy:
list.snippet: Low blood pressure is common during the first two trimesters of pregnancy.

list.title: Prolonged bed rest:
list.snippet: Lack of physical activity can weaken the cardiovascular system and contribute to hypotension.

list.title: Psychological factors:
list.snippet: Emotional stress can also play a role in some cases.

text_blocks.snippet: It's important to consult with a healthcare professional if you experience symptoms of low blood pressure to determine the underlying cause and receive appropriate treatment.
